intent.raw_query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers the most authentic Roman culinary experience away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a baroque villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited to 360 visitors at a time, ensuring an unhurried, immersive experience with masterpieces like Apollo and Daphne.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, cured meats, and the famously divisive quinto quarto (offal dishes) that define true Roman cucina povera tradition.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Forum and Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. Combined with Colosseum entry, this archaeological complex offers unparalleled insight into Roman history and culture, with panoramic views over ruins that inspired Renaissance artists for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 16:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in the local area around the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the nearby Chateau Drive area to get your bearings. Explore the local strip malls and nearby streets. Visit a nearby grocery store (Walmart or Kroger on Shorter Ave) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and drinks to save money throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or airport snack — no budget needed
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport food before departure
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A on Shorter Ave NW (within 2 miles of hotel) — budget-friendly fast casual, approx. $8–$12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Keep spending minimal. Buy breakfast items at the grocery store tonight to save on Day 2 morning costs. Rome, GA sits near the Coosa River and has a charming small-city feel — very different from Rome, Italy, but worth exploring on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a self-prepared breakfast from grocery store items in your hotel room. Head to Myrtle Hill Cemetery (free, 10 min drive) — a stunning hilltop historic cemetery with panoramic views of Rome, GA and the confluence of the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers. This is a beloved local landmark with beautiful art-inspired monuments and Civil War history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (approx. $8 admission) on Riverside Parkway — a National Historic Landmark exploring Cherokee history and culture with fascinating artifacts and art. Afterward, walk along the Riverwalk along the Oostanaula River (free) for scenic views and fresh air. Stop at the Rome Area History Museum on Broad Street (free or low-cost admission) for local art and cultural exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Downtown Rome on Broad Street — a walkable, charming downtown strip with local shops and restaurants. Browse local art galleries if any are open late. Enjoy the Clock Tower plaza area.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in hotel room — cereal, fruit, yogurt from grocery store (~$2–$3)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café on Broad Street NW — local favorite with affordable sandwiches and salads (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad Street — casual deli-style dining with hearty portions (~$10–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Weather expected around 29.8°C — carry water and wear light clothing. Morning visits to outdoor sites are best before peak afternoon heat. Myrtle Hill is free and one of the most scenic spots in Rome, GA.

day_by_day.morning: Hotel breakfast or self-prepared meal. Drive to Berry College (free to visit campus) — one of the world's largest college campuses with stunning Gothic architecture, rolling hills, and free-roaming deer. The Ford Buildings and Mountain Campus are architecturally beautiful and feel like an open-air art museum. Bring a camera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Rome Little Theatre or check local listings for any afternoon art exhibitions or gallery openings at the Coosa Valley Art Center on East 2nd Avenue — a community art hub with rotating exhibits (free or low-cost). Browse local artisan shops on Broad Street for handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Friday night in Downtown Rome — check for live music events at local venues. The downtown area often has free outdoor events in summer. Walk the Broad Street corridor and enjoy the small-city nightlife atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast (~$2–$3)
meals.lunch: Partridge Restaurant on Broad Street or a local food truck near downtown (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: El Zarape Mexican Restaurant — generous portions, authentic flavors, very budget-friendly (~$9–$13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is a must-see — completely free to explore and genuinely breathtaking. Go early morning before the heat peaks. Check the Coosa Valley Art Center website or Facebook page for current exhibits before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Pack a light picnic and head to Coosa River Whitewater Park (free to watch, low-cost kayak rentals available) for an active morning. The park features man-made whitewater features and is a great spot for outdoor recreation and people-watching. Alternatively, visit Lock and Dam Park on the Coosa River for a peaceful nature walk (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rome Farmers Market (Saturday mornings through early afternoon) on the Riverwalk area — sample local Georgia produce, artisan foods, honey, jams, and handmade crafts. This is a great way to experience local food culture on a budget. Stock up on fresh fruit and snacks for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel pool (La Quinta typically has a pool) during the hottest part of the day. In the evening, take a scenic drive along the Coosa River corridor or visit Nob Hill area for views of the city at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared or grab a pastry and coffee from a local bakery (~$4–$6)
meals.lunch: Picnic from Farmers Market finds — local bread, cheese, fruit, and snacks (~$8–$10 total)
meals.dinner: DaVinci's Pizzeria on Broad Street — wood-fired pizza in a casual setting, great value (~$10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the best day for the Farmers Market — arrive by 9–10 AM for the best selection. The whitewater park is free to visit and very photogenic. Afternoon heat will be intense (~30°C) so the hotel pool break is a smart budget-friendly activity.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to nearby Calhoun, GA (approx. 30 min drive) to visit the New Echota State Historic Site — the former capital of the Cherokee Nation, with reconstructed buildings, a museum, and significant cultural and artistic heritage. Admission is very low cost (~$5–$7). This is a deeply moving and educational experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return to Rome, stop at Barnsley Resort area in Adairsville (free to drive through the gardens area) or visit the Adairsville downtown antique shops for affordable art prints, vintage finds, and unique souvenirs. Alternatively, return to Rome and visit the Shorter University Art Gallery (free, call ahead to confirm Sunday hours).
day_by_day.evening: Quiet Sunday evening — cook a simple meal using groceries, or treat yourself to a sit-down dinner in downtown Rome. Enjoy the slower Sunday pace and rest up.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast (~$2–$3)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches from hotel room supplies for the day trip to save money, or grab fast food in Calhoun (~$7–$10)
meals.dinner: Applebee's or Longhorn Steakhouse on Shorter Ave — reliable budget-friendly chain options with Sunday specials (~$12–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: New Echota is one of the most historically significant sites in Georgia and is very undervisited — a hidden gem. Confirm opening hours before going (typically closed Mondays, so Sunday is ideal). Gas for the day trip will be the main cost — roughly $5–$8 round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Area Council for the Arts or check for any free public art installations around downtown Rome. Walk the public art trail along Broad Street — Rome has invested in public murals and sculptures throughout the downtown corridor. This is a completely free self-guided art walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Cave Spring, GA (approx. 20 min from Rome) — a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park, very low admission ~$2–$3), a natural spring, a public swimming pool, and beautiful historic architecture. The cave is a unique geological art of nature and the town is extremely photogenic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final proper downtown dinner. Browse any remaining shops or galleries on Broad Street. Pick up any last souvenirs or local food products (Georgia pecans, local honey, etc.) as gifts.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hotel room breakfast (~$2–$3)
meals.lunch: Grab a bite in Cave Spring — small local diner or pack a lunch (~$6–$10)
meals.dinner: Harvest Moon Café or a return visit to a favorite from earlier in the week (~$10–$15)

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a truly magical hidden gem — the cave, spring, and historic town square are all within walking distance of each other. The natural swimming pool fed by the spring is refreshing on a hot June day. Bring cash as some small vendors may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast or self-prepared meal. Take one last walk or drive through downtown Rome to soak in the atmosphere. Visit any spots you may have missed — the Clock Tower, the Romulus and Remus wolf statue (a gift from Rome, Italy — a fun connection!), and the scenic river confluence viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta by Wyndham. Depending on departure time, visit a final local food spot for a proper Southern lunch as a farewell meal. Head to the airport or begin your journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home. Reflect on a wonderful budget-friendly week exploring Rome, GA's art, food, history, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared or hotel complimentary breakfast if available (~$0–$3)
meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company or a local Southern diner for a farewell meal (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Airport or travel food as needed

day_by_day.notes: Rome's wolf statue near the clock tower is a direct gift from Rome, Italy and a wonderful photo opportunity — a fun full-circle moment for a trip named after the Italian capital. Total estimated budget for the 7-day trip (excluding flights and hotel): approximately $150–$220 per person, covering meals, admissions, and local transport.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (15 Chateau Drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings and shake off any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first-night dinner close to the hotel. Explore a nearby casual Italian-American trattoria or local restaurant within walking distance of the property. Keep the evening relaxed — enjoy a glass of wine and a simple pasta dish to ease into the trip.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (grab a snack at the airport if needed)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel – look for a neighborhood Italian restaurant or trattoria offering pasta, salad, and house wine. Budget approx. $20–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 16:00, Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and hydration after travel. Confirm any pre-booked experience reservations for the days ahead. Note: La Quinta by Wyndham Rome is located in Rome, Georgia, USA (34.2212, -85.1513), so all itinerary activities are planned around the Rome, Georgia area and its surroundings, not Rome, Italy. Adjust dining and activity logistics accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a hearty breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then head out for a morning visit to a local art museum or cultural center in the Rome, GA area — the Chieftains Museum & Major Ridge Home is a great historically rich option, offering insight into Cherokee heritage and early American history. Arrive early (around 9:00–9:30 AM) to beat the heat (highs near 30°C expected).
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Rome Area History Museum or browse the local galleries along Broad Street in downtown Rome, GA. The downtown area has a charming walkable arts district with independent galleries and boutique shops. Spend 2–3 hours exploring at a comfortable pace, ducking into air-conditioned spaces during the hottest part of the day (1:00–3:00 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience (adapted to a local food and wine evening tour if available in the area, or replicate the spirit by visiting a local wine bar and sampling regional appetizers). Alternatively, book a food-focused evening at a well-reviewed downtown Rome, GA restaurant featuring Southern or Italian-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café – try eggs, toast, and coffee. Budget approx. $10–15.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a downtown Rome, GA eatery – sandwiches, salads, or Southern comfort food. Budget approx. $12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner at a downtown restaurant – look for Italian-American options or farm-to-table Southern cuisine with wine pairings. Budget approx. $25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing given the ~30°C heat. Carry water and sunscreen. Downtown Rome, GA is approximately 10–15 minutes from the hotel by car.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel experience (if this is a virtual/traveling exhibition available locally, or plan a day trip to Atlanta, ~75 miles away, to visit the High Museum of Art for a world-class art collection experience). Arrive at opening time (around 9:00–9:30 AM) to maximize time before the afternoon heat peaks. Spend 2.5–3 hours immersed in art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the museum or gallery through early afternoon, then find a nearby café or restaurant for a relaxed lunch. After lunch, visit a second gallery space or take a self-guided walking tour of public art installations in the area. If in Atlanta, explore Midtown's arts corridor before heading back toward Rome, GA in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome, GA by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local mid-range restaurant. Try a place with a good wine list to wind down after a full day of art and culture.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a local bakery – pastry, fruit, and coffee. Budget approx. $8–12.
meals.lunch: Museum café or nearby bistro – soup, sandwich, or salad. Budget approx. $15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner in Rome, GA – Italian or American cuisine with a glass of wine. Budget approx. $25–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If traveling to Atlanta for the High Museum of Art, allow 1.5 hours each way by car. Purchase museum tickets online in advance to avoid queues. The High Museum regularly hosts traveling international exhibitions that may align with the Vatican Museums theme.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour experience – visit a local fine arts gallery or sculpture garden in the Rome, GA region. The Shorter University campus or Berry College (one of the largest college campuses in the world, located just outside Rome, GA) offers beautiful grounds and occasional art exhibitions. Arrive by 9:00 AM for a cool morning walk through the scenic campus landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour spirit – explore the Rome, GA Farmers Market (held on Saturdays at the Forum River Center) for local produce, artisan foods, and regional specialties. Chat with vendors, sample local jams, cheeses, and baked goods. This is a great way to connect with the local food culture in an authentic, budget-friendly way.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience – replicate this by planning a self-guided evening food walk through downtown Rome, GA. Visit 2–3 restaurants or bars for small plates and drinks: start with appetizers at one spot, move to a wine bar for a glass and charcuterie, and finish with dessert at a local bakery or ice cream shop.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Farmers Market – fresh pastries, fruit, and local coffee. Budget approx. $8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch using market finds or at a casual downtown café. Budget approx. $10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Progressive dinner across 2–3 downtown spots – small plates, wine, and dessert. Budget approx. $30–45 per person total.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day for the Farmers Market (check current hours – typically 8:00 AM–12:00 PM). The evening food walk works best if you make loose reservations or check wait times at popular spots. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk experience – visit the Mound Cemetery in Rome, GA (a National Historic Landmark with ancient Native American burial mounds) for a meaningful archaeological and historical morning walk. Alternatively, drive to Etowah Indian Mounds State Historic Site in Cartersville, GA (~45 minutes away) for a more immersive ancient history experience with museum exhibits and mound walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the archaeological site, stop for lunch in Cartersville or head back toward Rome, GA. In the afternoon, visit a local antique market or art studio for a relaxed, creative afternoon. Many artists in the Rome, GA area open their studios on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet Sunday evening dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant. Opt for a place with outdoor seating if the temperature has cooled (evenings in June in Georgia can be pleasant after 7:00 PM). Try a restaurant offering Southern cuisine with a creative twist.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local diner – eggs, biscuits, and coffee in true Southern style. Budget approx. $10–15.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near the archaeological site or back in Rome, GA – burgers, sandwiches, or Southern plates. Budget approx. $12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Mid-range Sunday dinner – Southern comfort food or Italian-American cuisine with dessert. Budget approx. $25–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Etowah Indian Mounds is open Tuesday–Sunday; confirm hours before visiting. Bring sunscreen and water for outdoor mound walks in the heat. The site has a small but excellent museum included with admission (~$5–7 per person).

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a cooking or food experience – book a local cooking class in Rome, GA or the greater Northwest Georgia area, focusing on Italian or Southern cuisine. Alternatively, visit a local specialty food shop or Italian deli to pick up ingredients and learn about regional food culture from the proprietors. This ties directly into the food interest theme of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rome Area Council for the Arts or a local pottery/ceramics studio for an afternoon art activity. Many studios offer drop-in workshops where you can try your hand at a craft. This is a fun, hands-on way to engage with the local arts scene. Budget approx. $25–40 for a workshop session.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory penultimate-night dinner at one of Rome, GA's best mid-range restaurants. Dress up slightly and enjoy a full three-course meal with wine. Look for a restaurant with a strong local reputation and a menu that highlights seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast – avocado toast, eggs, or a smoothie bowl at a local coffee shop. Budget approx. $10–14.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local bistro or sandwich shop after the morning food experience. Budget approx. $12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at a top-rated local restaurant – appetizer, entrée, dessert, and wine. Budget approx. $40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings for any Monday evening art openings or food events in downtown Rome, GA – June is an active month for community events. Book the dinner reservation in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a favorite café discovered during the trip. Take a last stroll through downtown Rome, GA to pick up any souvenirs, local food products (jams, hot sauces, local honey), or art prints from a gallery. Visit the Clock Tower at the top of the hill for a panoramic view of the city as a memorable farewell moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final lunch at a downtown restaurant. If time allows, make one last stop at a local art gallery or bookshop before heading to the airport or continuing your journey.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or travel onward. If staying an extra evening, enjoy a casual, low-key dinner at a neighborhood spot – keep it simple and reflective after a full week of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed final breakfast – full spread at the hotel or a beloved local café. Budget approx. $10–15.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a downtown Rome, GA favorite – try something you haven't had yet during the trip. Budget approx. $15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner if still in town – soup, salad, or a casual plate at a neighborhood restaurant. Budget approx. $15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for checkout and any last-minute packing. Keep receipts for any art or food purchases for customs if traveling internationally afterward. Reflect on highlights of the trip and note favorite spots for a return visit.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome's airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) whisks you to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to orient yourself and shake off any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join an intimate guided evening tour through Trastevere's cobblestone streets, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local wines, and cured meats at artisan stops. The golden-hour light on the medieval facades makes this a magical introduction to Rome.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (enjoy airline meal or airport lounge)
meals.dinner: Conclude the Trastevere food walk with a sit-down dinner at Ristorante Paris (Trastevere) – a refined Roman trattoria celebrated for cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and an excellent regional wine list. Reserve a terrace table in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private airport transfer and the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk before departure. Pack a light layer for the evening as temperatures can drop slightly after sunset. Keep luggage light for the evening walk.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Begin with an exclusive early-access skip-the-line guided tour (book a premium 'before opening' slot for 8:00 AM entry). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling with far fewer crowds than midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber to the elegant Prati neighborhood for a post-museum espresso and gelato at Gelateria dei Gracchi. Then visit St. Peter's Basilica and climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome (pre-book timed entry). Spend the late afternoon browsing the upscale boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then head to the historic center for an aperitivo at a rooftop bar such as Il Sorpasso or the terrace of Hotel Raphael for Campari spritzes with views of the Pantheon skyline.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning pastry at Caffè San Pietro near the Vatican – try the cornetto al pistacchio.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Il Sorpasso (Prati) – a beloved Roman bistro with excellent charcuterie boards, seasonal pasta, and natural wines. Ideal for a relaxed post-museum meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Il Matriciano (Prati) – a classic Roman institution near the Vatican, beloved for its bucatini all'amatriciana, abbacchio al forno, and warm, old-school atmosphere. Pair with a Cesanese del Piglio.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums early-access tickets at least 4–6 weeks in advance – they sell out fast, especially in June. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees required. Carry a small bottle of water; June heat (≈30°C) can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Take a private taxi or Uber to the Villa Borghese park for a premium guided tour of the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly timed to 2-hour slots; book well in advance). Marvel at Bernini's Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina, and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in an intimate, uncrowded setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Descend via the Spanish Steps to the Tridente district and explore the luxury shopping streets of Via Condotti (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi) and Via del Babuino.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at Stravinskij Bar inside the iconic Hotel de Russie – one of Rome's most glamorous garden bars, beloved by artists and celebrities. Sip a Negroni among jasmine-scented terraces.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Antico Caffè Greco on Via Condotti – Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), frequented by Keats, Byron, and Goethe. Order a cappuccino and maritozzo con la panna.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Nino (Tridente) – a Florentine-Roman institution near the Spanish Steps, known for bistecca, ribollita, and an excellent Tuscan wine cellar. A favorite of the Roman intelligentsia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Imàgo, the Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant of Hotel Hassler at the top of the Spanish Steps. Expect creative Italian haute cuisine with breathtaking panoramic views of Rome at dusk. Jacket recommended; reserve weeks ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be reserved in advance – only 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. Arrive 15 minutes early or you forfeit entry. The gallery is closed Mondays. Wear comfortable shoes for the park walk and shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Join a premium small-group or private guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Walk where Julius Caesar, Augustus, and Cicero once trod. A knowledgeable archaeologist-guide brings the ruins to life with vivid storytelling. Book a 9:00 AM slot to beat the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Forum, visit the nearby Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums) to see the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping views over the Forum from the terrace. Then cool off with a gelato at Fatamorgana (artisan, gluten-free flavors) near Campo de' Fiori.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric Campo de' Fiori market square at dusk (vendors pack up by afternoon, but the piazza buzzes with aperitivo life by evening). Stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning espresso at Caffè Tazza d'Oro near the Pantheon – famous for its granita di caffè con panna in summer.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Pierluigi (Campo de' Fiori area) – a beloved upscale seafood restaurant with a beautiful outdoor terrace. Try the spaghetti alle vongole and grilled branzino.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Pagliaccio – Rome's two-Michelin-starred gem near Campo de' Fiori. Chef Anthony Genovese crafts a boundary-pushing tasting menu blending Italian tradition with Asian influences. One of Rome's most extraordinary dining experiences. Reserve 4–6 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The Forum and Palatine Hill share a combined ticket; add the Colosseum for a full combo. Start early (9:00 AM) to avoid peak heat and crowds. Wear sunscreen and a hat. Il Pagliaccio requires formal attire and advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive into Rome's most authentic culinary neighborhood with a premium guided food tour of the Mercato Testaccio. Taste supplì al telefono, porchetta, aged pecorino, artisanal pasta, and the neighborhood's famous offal specialties (trippa, coda). Your guide provides cultural context for each tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, visit the nearby Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) – a hauntingly beautiful garden cemetery where Keats and Shelley are buried, beloved by artists and writers. Then explore the Aventine Hill: visit the Knights of Malta keyhole (perfectly framing St. Peter's dome) and the serene Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with its panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest during the hottest part of the afternoon. As the sun sets, take a private sunset boat tour on the Tiber River for a unique perspective of Rome's bridges and monuments from the water.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the food tour (you'll be eating plenty on the tour).
meals.lunch: The Testaccio Food Tour serves as a substantial late-morning/lunch experience. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Flavio al Velavevodetto – a legendary Testaccio trattoria carved into the Monte dei Cocci (ancient amphora hill), serving Roman classics like rigatoni con pajata and carciofi alla giudia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Roscioli – a celebrated Roman deli-restaurant near Campo de' Fiori, famous for its extraordinary wine cellar (2,800+ labels), house-cured meats, and exceptional carbonara. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Tuesday–Sunday mornings; Sunday can be lively. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Tiber boat tour should be pre-booked; sunset slots fill quickly in June. Roscioli is extremely popular – reserve at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art Studio & Artisan Workshop – Arrange a private visit to a Roman artist's studio or a luxury artisan workshop (mosaic-making, fresco painting, or leather-bound bookbinding in the tradition of Roman craftsmen). Several ateliers near the historic center offer bespoke 2–3 hour sessions for premium guests. Alternatively, revisit the Pantheon at opening time (9:00 AM) for a contemplative, crowd-free experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-visited but stunning Palazzo Doria Pamphilj – a private aristocratic palace still owned by the Pamphilj family, housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. The audio guide is narrated by a current family member. Afterward, wander the elegant Via del Corso for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert at a historic venue – Rome offers summer concerts in churches, courtyards, and villas throughout June. Options include concerts at the Oratorio del Gonfalone or outdoor performances at Villa Giulia. Dress elegantly for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Pasticceria Regoli near the Esquilino – a historic Roman pastry shop (est. 1916) celebrated for its maritozzi con la panna and seasonal fruit tarts.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca Corsi near the Pantheon – a charming, no-frills Roman lunch spot with a handwritten daily menu of traditional dishes like pasta e ceci and saltimbocca alla romana. Beloved by locals.
meals.dinner: Farewell-eve dinner at La Pergola – Rome's only three-Michelin-starred restaurant, perched atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel with sweeping panoramic views. Chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu is a transcendent experience. Formal dress required; reserve 6–8 weeks in advance. This is the pinnacle of Roman fine dining.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Rome's dining scene – if you can only book one special dinner, make it this one. Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is closed Thursdays. The artisan workshop should be arranged through your hotel concierge at least 3–4 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – Visit the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (GNAM) in the Villa Borghese park for a quieter, world-class collection of 19th and 20th century Italian and international art (Klimt, Cézanne, Modigliani). Alternatively, spend a slow morning at the Piazza del Popolo: visit the twin baroque churches and the Church of Santa Maria del Popolo (Caravaggio's Conversion of Saint Paul).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Via Condotti or Via Borgognona – pick up artisan gifts: a silk scarf from Battistoni, leather goods from Sermoneta Gloves, or bespoke stationery from Campo Marzio Design. Visit a high-end enoteca such as Trimani (Rome's oldest wine shop, est. 1821) to select bottles of Barolo or Brunello to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport via pre-arranged private luxury transfer. Enjoy a final espresso at the airport lounge before your flight.

meals.breakfast: A slow, indulgent final breakfast at the hotel. Request a room-service spread or dine in the hotel restaurant with fresh pastries, fruit, and a proper cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Osteria Barberini near the Trevi Fountain – a refined Roman osteria with excellent cacio e pepe, artichoke dishes, and a curated wine list. Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain afterward for good luck and a return to Rome.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or in-flight, depending on departure time. Ask your hotel concierge to prepare a luxury picnic box with Roman specialties (prosciutto, aged pecorino, supplì, local wine) if your flight departs in the evening.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Rome's Fiumicino (FCO) airport. Pre-arrange the return private transfer the night before. Confirm all luggage weight limits if purchasing wine or artisan goods. Keep a small amount of euros for tips and last-minute purchases.
